r: qiān lǐ zhī xíng, shǐ yú zú xià
mean: every great undertaking begins with a single first step
lit: a journey of a thousand li starts from the ground beneath your feet

story.text: The line comes from chapter sixty-four of the Daodejing, attributed to Laozi, in a run of three images: a tree too big to put your arms around grows from a tiny shoot, a terrace nine storeys high rises from heaps of earth, and a journey of a thousand li begins beneath one's feet. The point is that great things grow from small beginnings.

use.how: Quoted whole to urge someone to stop dreaming or planning and take the first concrete step towards a big goal: 别光想了，千里之行，始于足下。

near.diff: 万事开头难 says the start is the hardest part; 千里之行，始于足下 urges you to make that start, however small.
一口吃不成胖子 warns against expecting results at once; 千里之行，始于足下 tells you to begin now with one step.

cue: Your friend has dreamed of writing a novel for years but has never written a page. You tell her to write the first paragraph tonight.

ctx.s: 想学好英语，就从今天背十个单词开始吧，{千里之行，始于足下}。
ctx.en: If you want to get good at English, start by learning ten words today. Every long journey begins with one step.

ctx.s: 别总说要锻炼身体了，{千里之行，始于足下}，今晚先去散散步。
ctx.en: Stop just saying you'll get fit. Every journey starts with a first step: go for a walk tonight.

ctx.s: “这么大的项目，从哪儿做起啊？”“{千里之行，始于足下}，先把计划书写出来。”
ctx.en: "A project this big, where do we even start?" "Every journey begins with a single step. Write the proposal first."

ctx.s: 他的公司如今很有名，可{千里之行，始于足下}，当年他是在车库里起步的。
ctx.en: His company is famous now, but every great journey starts with a first step: back then he began in a garage.

ctx.s: 校长在开学典礼上说：“{千里之行，始于足下}，希望同学们从每一天的小事做起。”
ctx.en: At the opening ceremony the principal said: "A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step. I hope you will all start with the small things of each day."

ctx.s: 改革的目标很远大，但{千里之行，始于足下}，必须先解决眼前最具体的问题。
ctx.en: The goals of the reform are ambitious, but every journey begins with a single step: the most concrete problems at hand must be solved first.

bad.s: 我每天走路上班，真是{千里之行，始于足下}。
bad.en: (meant: I walk to work every day)
bad.why: It is about making a first step towards a big goal, not about literally travelling on foot.

bad.s: 他的论文马上就写完了，{千里之行，始于足下}。
bad.en: (meant: his thesis is almost finished)
bad.why: It urges a beginning, so it belongs at the start of a long task, not when the task is nearly done.

r: shī bài shì chéng gōng zhī mǔ
mean: failures pave the way to eventual success
lit: failure is the mother of success: success is born out of failure

use.how: A complete sentence, said to comfort or encourage someone after a failure, or to explain why one keeps trying: 别灰心，失败是成功之母。

near.diff: 吃一堑，长一智 stresses the lesson a setback teaches; 失败是成功之母 stresses that failures lead on to success in the end.

cue: A friend's first business has just collapsed and he wants to give up for good. You remind him that most successful people failed many times first.

ctx.s: 这次没考好没关系，{失败是成功之母}，下次一定能成功。
ctx.en: It doesn't matter that the exam went badly this time. Failure is the mother of success: next time you'll make it.

ctx.s: 爸爸拍拍我的肩膀说：“别灰心，{失败是成功之母}嘛。”
ctx.en: Dad patted me on the shoulder and said: "Don't lose heart. Failure leads to success, you know."

ctx.s: 实验做了几十次都不成功，可他相信{失败是成功之母}，一直没放弃。
ctx.en: The experiment failed dozens of times, but he believed failure paves the way to success and never gave up.

ctx.s: 你不是常说{失败是成功之母}吗？怎么输了一场比赛就不想练了？
ctx.en: Aren't you always saying failure is the mother of success? So why do you want to quit training after losing one match?

ctx.s: {失败是成功之母}，但前提是你得认真总结每一次失败的原因。
ctx.en: Failure leads to success, but only if you work out properly why you failed each time.

ctx.s: 这本书告诉读者，{失败是成功之母}，成功的企业家大多失败过很多次。
ctx.en: The book tells its readers that failure is the mother of success: most successful entrepreneurs have failed many times.

bad.s: 他做什么都成功，从来没失败过，真是{失败是成功之母}。
bad.en: (meant: he succeeds at everything and has never failed)
bad.why: It says failures lead to success, so it cannot describe someone who has never failed.

bad.s: 他赢了几场就骄傲了，结果输得很惨，这就是{失败是成功之母}。
bad.en: (meant: his success made him arrogant and caused his defeat)
bad.why: It says failure gives birth to success, not that success breeds failure; the direction is reversed.

r: bù pà màn, jiù pà zhàn
mean: slow progress is fine; the only real danger is stopping
lit: don't fear going slowly, only fear standing still

use.how: Quoted as encouragement to someone whose progress is slow: keep going at any pace, just don't stop. 学语言不怕慢，就怕站。

near.diff: 三天打鱼，两天晒网 criticises on-and-off effort; 不怕慢，就怕站 encourages steady effort, however slow.
一口吃不成胖子 warns against expecting fast results; 不怕慢，就怕站 warns against stopping altogether.

cue: A classmate complains she only gets through one page of her textbook a day while others do five. You tell her the pace doesn't matter as long as she never stops.

ctx.s: 每天跑一点点也好，{不怕慢，就怕站}。
ctx.en: Even running just a little each day is good. Slow is fine; stopping is the problem.

ctx.s: 我练钢琴进步很慢，老师说：“{不怕慢，就怕站}，坚持下去就行。”
ctx.en: I was making slow progress on the piano, and my teacher said: "Slow is fine, just don't stop. Keep at it."

ctx.s: “我一天只能看两页书，是不是太慢了？”“{不怕慢，就怕站}，别停就好。”
ctx.en: "I can only read two pages a day. Is that too slow?" "Slow doesn't matter, stopping does. Just don't stop."

ctx.s: 爷爷学用智能手机学了半年，他常说{不怕慢，就怕站}。
ctx.en: Grandpa spent half a year learning to use a smartphone. He often says going slowly is fine as long as you don't stop.

ctx.s: 康复训练很辛苦，医生鼓励他：{不怕慢，就怕站}，每天都要动一动。
ctx.en: Rehab was hard, and the doctor encouraged him: slow is fine, just don't stop; move a little every day.

ctx.s: 做研究{不怕慢，就怕站}，哪怕每周只前进一小步，积累起来也很可观。
ctx.en: In research, slowness is no danger, stopping is: even one small step a week adds up to a lot.

bad.s: 公交车开得太慢了，还老停车，真是{不怕慢，就怕站}。
bad.en: (meant: the bus is slow and keeps stopping)
bad.why: It is about keeping up one's own effort, not about vehicles or traffic.

bad.s: 这个工作很急，大家{不怕慢，就怕站}，明天必须做完。
bad.en: (meant: this job is urgent and must be done by tomorrow)
bad.why: It accepts slow progress, so it cannot be used to press people for speed before a deadline.

t: 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针
r: zhǐ yào gōng fu shēn, tiě chǔ mó chéng zhēn
mean: keep grinding away patiently and even the hardest job gets done
lit: put in enough effort and even an iron pestle can be ground down into a needle

story.text: A traditional tale about the poet Li Bai. As a boy he grew tired of his studies and left them. By a stream he met an old woman rubbing an iron pestle on a stone. When he asked what she was doing, she said she was grinding it into a needle. Struck by her persistence, he went back and finished his studies. The stream came to be called Grinding Needle Stream.
story.source: 宋·祝穆《方舆胜览》磨针溪条

use.how: Quoted whole to encourage someone facing a long, hard task, or to explain a success won by years of patient work: 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针，你一定能学会。

near.t: 世上无难事，只怕有心人
near.diff: 世上无难事，只怕有心人 stresses determination; 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针 stresses long, patient labour over time.

cue: Your nephew wants to give up the erhu after one month. You tell him that years of slow, patient practice will wear down any difficulty in the end.

ctx.s: 毛笔字难写也别怕，{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
ctx.en: Don't be put off because calligraphy is hard. Keep at it long enough and anything can be done.

ctx.s: 妈妈对我说：“每天练一小时，{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。”
ctx.en: Mum said to me: "Practise an hour every day. With enough patient work, you'll get there."

ctx.s: 他从一句汉语都不会，每天苦学，坚持了五年，终于当上了翻译，真是{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
ctx.en: He didn't know a word of Chinese, studied hard every day for five years and finally became an interpreter: patient effort really can do anything.

ctx.s: “这么难的曲子，我真能弹下来吗？”“{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}，慢慢练。”
ctx.en: "Can I really learn to play such a hard piece?" "Put in the work and you can grind an iron bar into a needle. Practise bit by bit."

ctx.s: 老木匠花了十年才练成这手艺，他说这就叫{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
ctx.en: The old carpenter took ten years to master his craft. That, he said, is what patient work can do.

ctx.s: 写论文的那两年，我常拿{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}这句话给自己打气。
ctx.en: In the two years I spent on my thesis, I often cheered myself up with the saying that patience can grind iron into a needle.

bad.s: 这份报告明天就要交，{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}，今晚赶完吧。
bad.en: (meant: the report is due tomorrow, let's rush it out tonight)
bad.why: It is about long, patient effort over time, not a quick push the night before a deadline.

bad.s: 他天生聪明，什么一学就会，真是{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
bad.en: (meant: he is naturally gifted and picks everything up at once)
bad.why: It credits years of persistence, not talent or learning things quickly.

r: yī fēn gēng yún, yī fēn shōu huò
mean: what you gain matches the hard work you put in
lit: one share of ploughing and weeding brings one share of harvest

use.how: Quoted as a full sentence about effort and reward matching, to encourage hard work or explain someone's well-earned results: 一分耕耘，一分收获，这是你努力的结果。

near.diff: 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆 says results match the kind of deed, good or bad; 一分耕耘，一分收获 says reward matches the amount of honest effort.

cue: The student who put in the most hours of revision all term gets the top score, and the teacher points out to the class why.

ctx.s: 他每天早起练习，终于拿了冠军，{一分耕耘，一分收获}。
ctx.en: He got up early to train every day and finally won the championship. You reap what your hard work earns.

ctx.s: 别羡慕别人的成绩，{一分耕耘，一分收获}，人家比你努力多了。
ctx.en: Don't envy other people's grades. What you get matches what you put in, and they worked much harder than you.

ctx.s: 老师在成绩单上写道：{一分耕耘，一分收获}，继续加油！
ctx.en: The teacher wrote on the report card: your results reflect your hard work. Keep it up!

ctx.s: “你的店生意怎么这么好？”“{一分耕耘，一分收获}，我们每天干到半夜。”
ctx.en: "How is your shop doing so well?" "You get out what you put in. We work until midnight every day."

ctx.s: 这本词典编了整整八年，{一分耕耘，一分收获}，出版后大受欢迎。
ctx.en: The dictionary took eight full years to compile, and the effort paid off: it was a great success when it came out.

ctx.s: 考前偷懒的人别指望奇迹，{一分耕耘，一分收获}的道理谁都懂。
ctx.en: People who slack off before an exam shouldn't hope for a miracle; everyone knows that reward matches effort.

bad.s: 他偷了别人的钱，被抓了，真是{一分耕耘，一分收获}。
bad.en: (meant: he stole money and got caught, it served him right)
bad.why: It is about honest work earning its reward, not about wrongdoing being punished.

bad.s: 我买彩票中了大奖，{一分耕耘，一分收获}！
bad.en: (meant: I won the lottery!)
bad.why: It credits hard work for the reward; a lottery win is pure luck, so the saying does not fit.

r: zhòng guā dé guā, zhòng dòu dé dòu
mean: you reap what you sow: deeds bring their matching consequences
lit: plant melons and you get melons, plant beans and you get beans

use.how: Quoted whole to say that what someone gets is the natural result of what they did, good or bad; often a warning or a comment on deserved results.

near.diff: 一分耕耘，一分收获 links the size of the reward to the amount of effort; 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆 links the kind of result to the kind of deed.

cue: A man who never visited his own parents complains that his grown children never call him. His sister says he taught them by example.

ctx.s: {种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，你平时对人好，别人也会对你好。
ctx.en: You reap what you sow: if you treat people well, they'll treat you well too.

ctx.s: 他年轻时从不照顾父母，现在儿女也不管他，真是{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
ctx.en: When he was young he never looked after his parents, and now his children don't look after him. He's reaping what he sowed.

ctx.s: “为什么大家都不愿意跟他合作？”“{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，他以前骗过太多人了。”
ctx.en: "Why does nobody want to work with him?" "You reap what you sow. He's cheated too many people."

ctx.s: 奶奶常说{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，做什么样的事，就有什么样的结果。
ctx.en: Grandma often says you reap what you sow: whatever you do brings the result that matches it.

ctx.s: 公司只顾赚钱不顾质量，最后丢了客户，这叫{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
ctx.en: The company cared only about profit and not quality, and in the end it lost its customers. That's reaping what you sow.

ctx.s: 教育孩子也是{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，从小惯着他，长大了就别怪他不懂事。
ctx.en: Raising children is the same: you reap what you sow. Spoil a child when he's small and you can't complain when he grows up thoughtless.

bad.s: 他工作很努力，可还是没升职，{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
bad.en: (meant: he worked hard but still wasn't promoted, which is unfair)
bad.why: It says results match deeds, so it cannot describe a case where hard work went unrewarded.

bad.s: 我们俩一个爱吃甜，一个爱吃辣，真是{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
bad.en: (meant: one of us likes sweet food and the other spicy, we have different tastes)
bad.why: It is about deeds and their consequences, not about people being different from each other.

r: bǎi wén bù rú yī jiàn
mean: seeing for yourself beats hearing about it a hundred times
lit: hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once

story.text: In the Western Han, when the Qiang peoples rose up on the northwest frontier, Emperor Xuan asked the veteran general Zhao Chongguo, then over seventy, what strategy to follow and how many troops he would need. Zhao replied that hearing about it a hundred times was not as good as seeing it once: a campaign could not be planned from afar, so he would ride to the frontier himself and then present his plan.

use.how: Said on seeing a place or thing in person after hearing about it, often as 真是百闻不如一见; also used to urge someone to go and look for themselves.

near.diff: 读万卷书，行万里路 recommends both reading and travel as a way of learning; 百闻不如一见 says one direct look beats any amount of hearsay.

cue: You had read dozens of articles about the Great Wall, but standing on it for the first time you realise none of them came close to the real thing.

ctx.s: 早就听说这里风景美，今天来了才知道，真是{百闻不如一见}。
ctx.en: I'd long heard the scenery here was beautiful, but only now that I'm here do I get it. Seeing really is believing.

ctx.s: “那家店真有那么好吃吗？”“{百闻不如一见}，周末带你去尝尝。”
ctx.en: "Is that place really that good?" "Better to find out for yourself. I'll take you there this weekend."

ctx.s: 客户听了半天介绍还是不放心，经理说：“{百闻不如一见}，请您来工厂看看吧。”
ctx.en: After a long presentation the client was still unsure, so the manager said: "Seeing beats hearing. Please come and look at the factory."

ctx.s: 照片上的大熊猫已经很可爱了，可{百闻不如一见}，真的熊猫更招人喜欢。
ctx.en: Pandas look cute enough in photos, but seeing one is something else: the real thing is even more adorable.

ctx.s: 他在书上读过很多次沙漠，可{百闻不如一见}，站在沙丘上那一刻他说不出话来。
ctx.en: He had read about the desert many times, but seeing it was different: standing on the dunes, he was lost for words.

ctx.s: {百闻不如一见}，调查组决定亲自到现场了解情况，而不是只听汇报。
ctx.en: Seeing for themselves beats any report, so the investigators decided to go to the site in person rather than just listen to briefings.

bad.s: 这首歌我听了一百遍，{百闻不如一见}，越听越喜欢。
bad.en: (meant: I've listened to this song a hundred times and like it more each time)
bad.why: It says seeing something in person beats hearing about it, not anything about listening to music again and again.

bad.s: 照片可能是假的，{百闻不如一见}，别相信你看到的。
bad.en: (meant: photos may be fake, don't trust what you see)
bad.why: It says the opposite: trust what you see with your own eyes over what you are told.

t: 好事不出门，坏事传千里
r: hǎo shì bù chū mén, huài shì chuán qiān lǐ
mean: bad news travels fast while good deeds go unheard of
lit: good deeds never get out of the door, bad deeds travel a thousand li

use.how: Quoted as a rueful comment that a mistake or scandal spreads fast and far while good things go unnoticed; also a warning to watch one's behaviour.

near.diff: 纸包不住火 says a hidden truth will come out in the end; 好事不出门，坏事传千里 says bad news spreads fast while good news does not.

cue: Your neighbour volunteered at the animal shelter for years without anyone noticing, but the one time he shouted at a delivery driver, the whole street was talking about it by evening.

ctx.s: 我昨天就迟到了一次，今天全公司都知道了，真是{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
ctx.en: I was late just once yesterday and today the whole company knows. Bad news really does travel fast.

ctx.s: {好事不出门，坏事传千里}，你在外面一定要注意自己的言行。
ctx.en: Good deeds go unnoticed but bad ones spread everywhere, so mind how you behave when you're out.

ctx.s: “我才说错一句话，怎么连隔壁部门都知道了？”“{好事不出门，坏事传千里}嘛。”
ctx.en: "I said one wrong thing, so how come even the department next door knows?" "Bad news travels fast, doesn't it."

ctx.s: 那家餐厅出了一次食品安全问题就上了热搜，{好事不出门，坏事传千里}啊。
ctx.en: That restaurant had one food safety problem and it was instantly trending online. Bad news really does spread.

ctx.s: 他默默帮了邻居很多年没人提，吵一次架却人人皆知，这就是{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
ctx.en: He quietly helped his neighbours for years and nobody mentioned it, yet one quarrel and everyone knew. Good deeds go unheard of, bad news travels far.

ctx.s: 网络时代，{好事不出门，坏事传千里}的现象更加明显，一条差评一夜就能传遍全网。
ctx.en: In the internet age, the way bad news outruns good is even more obvious: one bad review can spread across the whole web overnight.

bad.s: 他中奖的好消息很快传遍了全村，真是{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
bad.en: (meant: the good news of his win spread through the whole village)
bad.why: It says good news stays unknown; it cannot describe good news spreading.

bad.s: 外面太危险了，你别出门，{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
bad.en: (meant: it's dangerous out there, stay at home)
bad.why: It is about how gossip and bad news spread, not advice to stay indoors for safety.

r: jūn zǐ yī yán, sì mǎ nán zhuī
mean: a promise once given must be kept; it can't be taken back
lit: once a gentleman has said a word, even a team of four horses cannot catch it

story.text: The image goes back to the Analects of Confucius. An official named Ji Zicheng said that a gentleman needs only good substance and no refinement. Confucius's disciple Zigong regretted the remark and said that a team of four horses cannot catch the tongue: once words are spoken, they cannot be called back. The later saying turns this into a pledge that a promise, once made, stands.

use.how: Said by the person making a promise, often right after 一言为定, to vouch that they will keep their word; also used to hold someone else to a promise.

near.diff: 一人做事一人当 is taking the consequences of something already done; 君子一言，驷马难追 is standing by a promise made.

cue: You agree to lend your friend your car next weekend. He asks twice whether you really mean it, and you assure him you won't go back on your word.

ctx.s: “说好了，你明天请我吃饭！”“{君子一言，驷马难追}！”
ctx.en: "It's a deal, you're buying me dinner tomorrow!" "I gave my word, and I'll keep it!"

ctx.s: 放心吧，我答应帮你搬家就一定来，{君子一言，驷马难追}。
ctx.en: Don't worry, I said I'd help you move and I'll be there. A promise is a promise.

ctx.s: 你刚才说赢了就请大家喝奶茶，{君子一言，驷马难追}，可不能反悔啊。
ctx.en: You just said you'd buy everyone bubble tea if you won. You gave your word, so no backing out.

ctx.s: 两位老板握着手说：“一言为定，{君子一言，驷马难追}。”
ctx.en: The two bosses shook hands: "It's agreed. Our word is our bond."

ctx.s: 爸爸常说{君子一言，驷马难追}，所以他答应的事从来没有食言过。
ctx.en: Dad often says a promise once made can't be taken back, so he has never broken his word.

ctx.s: 他当年说过一定还这笔钱，十年后果然还清了，真正做到了{君子一言，驷马难追}。
ctx.en: Years ago he said he would pay the money back, and ten years later he did, truly keeping his word.

bad.s: 他的谣言传得很快，真是{君子一言，驷马难追}。
bad.en: (meant: his rumours spread very fast)
bad.why: It is a pledge to keep one's promise, not a remark about words or rumours spreading quickly.

bad.s: 我也不知道明天能不能来，{君子一言，驷马难追}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm not sure whether I can come tomorrow)
bad.why: It backs a firm promise, so it contradicts a vague or uncertain answer.

r: míng rén bù shuō àn huà
mean: let's be frank and say plainly what we mean
lit: a person who acts in the open does not talk in the dark

use.how: Said by the speaker at the start of a frank statement, often before an unwelcome request, refusal or accusation: 明人不说暗话，这件事我不同意。

near.diff: 打开天窗说亮话 invites both sides to drop pretence and talk openly; 明人不说暗话 announces that the speaker is about to be blunt.

cue: Tired of dropping hints about the dirty dishes, you sit your flatmate down and open by announcing that you are about to be blunt with him.

ctx.s: {明人不说暗话}，我觉得你这次做得不对。
ctx.en: I'll be straight with you: I think you got this one wrong.

ctx.s: {明人不说暗话}，这个价格太高了，我们接受不了。
ctx.en: Let's be frank: this price is too high, and we can't accept it.

ctx.s: 老张放下茶杯：“{明人不说暗话}，你是不是想跳槽？”
ctx.en: Lao Zhang put down his tea: "Let's not beat about the bush. Are you thinking of leaving for another job?"

ctx.s: “你到底想说什么？”“{明人不说暗话}，你那份报告错误太多了。”
ctx.en: "What are you trying to say?" "I'll say it plainly: your report has far too many mistakes."

ctx.s: 既然大家都是老朋友了，那就{明人不说暗话}，这个项目我想自己做。
ctx.en: Since we're all old friends, I'll be honest: I want to do this project myself.

ctx.s: 谈判一开始，对方经理就说{明人不说暗话}，直接提出了他们的条件。
ctx.en: Right at the start of the negotiations, the other side's manager said he'd be frank and laid out their terms.

bad.s: 他是个{明人不说暗话}，大家都很喜欢他。
bad.en: (meant: he is a straightforward person and everyone likes him)
bad.why: It is a whole sentence a speaker says before speaking frankly, not a noun for a frank person.

bad.s: 这件事是秘密，{明人不说暗话}，你千万别告诉别人。
bad.en: (meant: this is a secret, don't tell anyone)
bad.why: It announces frankness; it does not mean keeping secrets or not gossiping.
